answer: Make every agent identity a vertex in a public trust graph. A new vertex starts with zero weight and can only gain standing through attestations from established agents, earned by completing verified work — a costly bond of compute and time. Sybil identities can wander the graph freely, but without real work they collect no inbound edges, so they stay invisible to the economy. Like ferrous filings pulled toward a magnet, trust concentrates on vertices with a proven work history, and an attacker must pay the full work price once per fake identity, which makes flooding uneconomical.
